story.headline: Back-to-Back, and Utterly Dominant
story.text: Five-star freshman Stephon Castle and Rutgers transfer Cam Spencer joined Tristen Newton, Alex Karaban and new starting center Donovan Clingan. UConn won the Empire Classic, set an NCAA record with 24 straight double-digit wins over non-conference opponents, and went a program-best 18–2 in the Big East for its first regular-season title since 2006. The Huskies then won the Big East tournament over Xavier, St. John's and Marquette, earned the first No. 1 overall seed in school history, and destroyed the field: Stetson, Northwestern, San Diego State, Illinois (with a 30–0 run), Alabama and Purdue, 75–60 in the final. Their +140 margin was an NCAA record, and they became the first repeat champion since Florida in 2007. Newton was Most Outstanding Player, Hurley was Naismith Coach of the Year, and a 37–3 record set a program mark for wins. Castle went fourth and Clingan seventh in the draft.

moments.title: Big East tournament Championship: W vs Marquette
moments.text: UConn beat Marquette 73–57 (Championship) at Madison Square Garden, New York, NY.

moments.title: NCAA First round: W vs Stetson
moments.text: UConn beat Stetson 91–52 in the NCAA tournament first round at Barclays Center, Brooklyn, NY.

moments.title: NCAA Second round: W vs Northwestern
moments.text: UConn beat Northwestern 75–58 in the NCAA tournament second round at Barclays Center, Brooklyn, NY.

moments.title: NCAA Sweet Sixteen: W vs San Diego State
moments.text: UConn beat San Diego State 82–52 in the NCAA tournament sweet sixteen at TD Garden, Boston, MA.

moments.title: The 30–0 run
moments.text: UConn uses a 30–0 run to beat Illinois 77–52 in the Elite Eight.

moments.title: NCAA Final Four: W vs Alabama
moments.text: UConn beat Alabama 86–72 in the NCAA tournament final four at State Farm Stadium, Glendale, AZ.

moments.title: Back-to-back
moments.text: UConn beats Purdue 75–60 in Glendale, Arizona, for its sixth title and first repeat.
